STEP 1 - Scene: A bowl of cooked porridge or oatmeal-style grain dish (pale, creamy, with small orange flecks, possibly carrot or pumpkin). Photographed from directly above (top-down), on a wooden board inside a frame.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White cereal bowl, roughly 15 cm in diameter (the rim spans roughly the width of the wooden board, which is about 5-6 cm wide, so the bowl is consistent with ~15 cm). Radius 7.5 cm. Vessel area = 3.14 x 7.5^2 ≈ 177 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) cooked oat/grain porridge, (2) small orange pieces (carrot or pumpkin bits) mixed in.

STEP 4 - Area: Porridge covers nearly the whole inner bowl, about 80% of the vessel area (≈142 cm^2). Orange bits are scattered within it, counted within the same area, roughly 5% (≈9 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: Porridge pile about 3 cm deep at center, tapering toward edges; using ~2.5 cm average height: 142 x 2.5 ≈ 355 ml. Carrot/pumpkin pieces: 9 cm^2 x 1 cm ≈ 9 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Porridge is a mashed/dense grain mixture, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml: 355 x 0.9 ≈ 320 g. Orange pieces: 9 x 0.6 ≈ 5 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked oat porridge (made with water) ≈ 70 kcal/100 g, so 320 g ≈ 224 kcal. Cooked carrot/pumpkin ≈ 30 kcal/100 g, so 5 g ≈ 2 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A cereal bowl of porridge holding roughly 320 g and about 225 kcal is plausible for a single serving of cooked oatmeal, and the total is consistent with what is visible.

Total: about 325 g, about 226 kcal.
